title: Magnetism and electromagnetism
scope: Use your school’s topic list to select the ideas you need. These are original practice questions with illustrative values and suggested self-marking guidance, not official Cambridge papers.

objectives.label: Distinguish magnetic materials and explain poles and magnetisation.
objectives.note: Avoid treating every metal as ferromagnetic; explain aligned magnetic regions and why cutting a magnet retains paired poles.

objectives.label: Explain compass directions using Earth’s field and local disturbances.
objectives.note: Distinguish geographic north from magnetic-pole terminology and a field model from a literal bar magnet inside Earth.

objectives.label: Describe magnetic fields produced by wires and coils.
objectives.note: Use conventional-current direction in the grip rule; explain effects of current, turns and an iron core.

objectives.label: Predict motor forces and explain the turning of a current-carrying coil.
objectives.note: Distinguish translation from a couple; explain current reversal and the different energy transfers of motors and generators.

objectives.label: Explain induction and calculate ideal-transformer voltage and current.
objectives.note: Require changing magnetic flux, distinguish induced voltage from current in an open circuit, and account for generator energy input.

objectives.label: Explain how electromagnetic signals travel between transmitter and receiver.
objectives.note: Distinguish radiating changing fields from steady-current models, compare light and radio, and account for finite propagation time.
